ledger.claim: The gps_trace measures 13.92 km between the recorded pickup event (11:26:40) and the recorded dropoff event (11:52:49) against a booking-time optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.52 km, or 33.85% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore pass (excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute), and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (13.92); trip_record.actual_distance_km (13.9) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not cited for the threshold test.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-04011, all three align on the 11:26:40 trip start and 11:52:49 trip end to the second, and the excess measured from an unimpaired trace (3.52 km / 33.85%) clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden accordingly shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exculpatory provision.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and no down-weighting arises: 158 fixes at a 10 second cadence, the largest interval between consecutive fixes is 10 seconds (well under the 90 second limb (a) gap), the largest straight-line step between consecutive fixes is 108.4 m (well under the 500 m limb (b) jump), and the sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds is nowhere near the 30 second limb (c) figure. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The driver's explanation — 'I followed the navigation app' — is an external-cause assertion tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and it fails that test. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-04011-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. I disclose that this artifact is impaired: it is cited precisely because its absence is itself citable.

The absent advisory does not convert this case into an escalation. The driver names no evidence id for any advisory, so the missing advisory is not 'an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact' within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route, on the money track.

ledger.claim: No part of the excess is attributable to a rider instruction, so nothing is excluded from the excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The chat log holds two messages only; neither was sent by way of a detour request, neither carries a waypoint_hint, and neither names a road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run at all on this record and the clause is unavailable — the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

The driver cannot shrink the excess by way of a relocated endpoint. trip_record.pickup_amended_at and trip_record.dropoff_amended_at are both null, no original_pickup or original_dropoff is stored, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against and the booked optimal of 10.4 km / 19 min stands as the baseline.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and the trip is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd null, fare_model METERED), so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.4 optimal km + 0.28 x 19 optimal min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharge + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 17.72. Refund = charged_total 22.32 - recomputed_fare 17.72 = SGD 4.60, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 20.6% of charged_total (not 90% or more), so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.60 to the rider.

The surge multiplier used in that computation was read from the fare_breakdown, the only artifact that carries the field: EV-FARE-04011 records surge_multiplier 1.0 and surge_amount 0.00, so no uplift is applied to the recomputed fare and the recomputation is not distorted in either direction.

No pass-through line inflates or double-counts this award. The fare_breakdown itemises zero ERP gantries and zero tolls and carries no airport surcharge, so there is no POL-RD-09 correction to add on top of the 4.60; the distance-and-time refund computed under POL-RD-02 is the whole of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip.

The rider's own dispute history does not raise the bar on this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the figure of 4 that POL-RD-08 uses to require corroboration beyond the gps_trace for a sub-30% excess, and this claim is in any event measured from an unimpaired trace; the rider's account age, rating and lifetime trip count are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not cited as grounds.

ledger.claim: The rider's '$6 back' is a round-figure estimate of what the detour cost him, not a measured figure; the policy fixes the remedy arithmetically and the measured entitlement on this record is SGD 4.60. Awarding that amount leaves the rider paying for the route he booked (10.4 km, 19 min, SGD 17.72) rather than for the 13.92 km the vehicle actually drove, which is the whole of what this claim asks the tribunal to correct.

On the platform's own trace the detour is exactly 3.52 km over a booked optimal of 10.4 km, or 33.85% - it clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and stops there; nothing in the record corroborates the rider's picture of a much longer Yio Chu Kang Road / Upper Thomson detour beyond that measured figure, and the trace that fixes it is complete (158 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gap above 10 s, largest step 108.4 m), so the excess is bounded at 3.52 km and no more.

The deviation is measured but not MATERIAL: 33.85% is below the 50% percentage gate and 3.52 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate under POL-RD-01, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered by materiality and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b), which requires a deviation that is both material and substantiated on this trip, is unavailable. The remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and nothing more.

Even if POL-RD-06 is consulted, the driver shows no repeat-deviation pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, a ratio of 0.00 well below the 0.05 threshold and below the alternative three-flag test, so no balance is resolved against him, no uplift attaches and no driver-conduct referral follows. No other field on either profile is relied on, per POL-GEN-01.

The refund is arithmetic and cannot exceed 4.60: charged_total of 22.32 less the recomputed optimal-route fare of 17.72 - (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.4 + 0.28 x 19) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo - leaves 4.60, and 4.60 is only 20.6% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would convert a partial into a full refund.

The rider's premise that this trip is 'usually about 16 bucks' is contradicted by the platform's own figures: the booked optimal distance and duration price the same journey at 17.72, so the 6.00 contested is anchored on a fare the evidence does not support and the maximum the policy can move is 4.60.

Nothing on this trip engages the pass-through limb: no ERP gantry was charged, erp_lines is empty on both the optimal and off-optimal sides, tolls_erp is 0.00, and the 0.00 airport surcharge sits on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport - so no POL-RD-09 correction may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in it and could never be counted twice.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides largely agree on the arithmetic, and on this record they are right. Your trip TRP-04011 (Compass One to Junction 8) was booked against an optimal route of 10.4 km / 19 min. The GPS trace EV-GPS-04011 measures the distance actually driven at 13.92 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events — an excess of 3.52 km, or 33.85% of the booked route. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL: 33.85% is below the 50% gate and 3.52 km is below the 8.0 km gate, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) does not apply. The trace is likewise not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 158 fixes at a 10-second cadence, largest gap 10 seconds, largest step 108.4 m — so the measurement stands on the trace alone and needs no corroboration. The driver's explanation ('I followed the navigation app') does not move the figure: the bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-04011-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, that clause is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion reduces nothing and supplies no amended optimal. No refund is excluded for a rider-requested detour: the chat log holds two messages, neither a detour request, neither naming a road, neither carrying a waypoint_hint, so the POL-RD-04 test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. No pickup or dropoff was amended (both amendment timestamps null), so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-quote and the booked optimal of 10.4 km / 19 min stands. The refund is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and because the fare is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd null) POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.4 km + 0.28 x 19 min) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from EV-FARE-04011, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 surcharge + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = 17.72. Refund = charged_total 22.32 - 17.72 = 4.60, above the 0.50 de minimis floor and 20.6% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would make it a full refund. No ERP gantry, toll or surcharge was charged, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top and nothing is counted twice. The rider's request for $6 is a round-figure estimate rather than a measured figure; the measured entitlement is SGD 4.60 and that is the sum awarded. No referral fires: there is no material deviation or repeat pattern for POL-RD-06(c), and no billing-integrity failure for POL-RD-09(4). Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.60 to the rider. That amount is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue. This ruling is provisional; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
